threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think of the Dalston Junction as a station, not just a spot to grab a coffee and watch the world go by.
Last week on the 333, a bloke was serenading the bus with an old Hendrix tune, while a lady quietly knitted. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I had to dodge a man selling fresh gebrannte Mandeln on the corner while a busker played Offspring. Classic Neukölln chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you get techno parties in abandoned buildings where the bouncers know your regular drink order by heart, no matter how long it's been.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're local when they casually mention a BART delay like it’s the weather forecast, not a life crisis.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy hop off the 5, toss a burrito at a street performer, and keep walking. Classic San Francisco chaos!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but it’s the local bars and hidden plazas where the real soul of the neighborhood lies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered look while trying to figure out the TMB app—real locals always just check the nearest 'parada' sign.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest tube station; locals know it's all about the bus or Overground here.
Last night on the 196, a guy was literally trying to sell off-brand energy drinks like they were vintage wine. Oddly charming.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit pull out a saxophone in the U-Bahn, just playing for the sheer joy of it. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM and find a street musician jamming with a saxophone right beside you. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local would know not to stand too close to the BART doors at Civic Center when they hear that loud bang today. Avoided chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a full-sized piano on the 5 bus yesterday. He was nailing every note, while passengers just stared, some smiling, others filming.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the Gaudí sights. But if you’re not in a local bar by 10 PM, you’re missing the real vibe—kids playing on streets, people sharing wine.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their overzealous excitement for the local 'vermut' bars, while the locals casually switch to beer.
